title: The Unsaid Silence
premise: Edmund Kavanagh, once the conservatory's most celebrated composition student, returns two decades after a scandal destroyed his career to work as its night janitor. When a radio broadcast airs a string quartet movement he recognizes as one written by his late mentor's daughter, Marta — a piece she played for him once and never recorded — he realizes someone is claiming her unfinished legacy. As he investigates the claimant, a rising composer named Ilse Brandt who studied under Marta's mother, Edmund must finally translate the sentence Marta left unsaid the night she died: that his silence, not her ambition, ended everything. The novel ends with Edmund performing her quartet publicly under both their names, choosing truth over the loyalty that kept him mute, and finding in the conservatory's students the family he refused for twenty years.
about_author: Freya Villalobos is a former cellist who left orchestral life to write about the people music leaves behind. She lives near a decommissioned conservatory and writes at night, when the practice rooms are empty.

chapters.title: The Tenant of Hall C
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. We meet him mopping the conservatory floors at night, invisible among the students who don't know he was once its prodigy. He treats the building like rented space, avoiding the practice rooms where his old life happened. Emotional beat: numbness mistaken for peace, and the first crack in it when a student plays a phrase he wrote at nineteen.

chapters.title: A Song That Was Never Recorded
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Driving home, the radio airs a quartet movement he knows was composed by Marta, his mentor's daughter, who died before recording anything. He nearly crashes. The announcer credits it to Ilse Brandt. Emotional beat: shock curdling into something hotter — grief with an accusation inside it.

chapters.title: The Mother's Archive
chapters.summary: Edmund visits Halina, Marta's aging mother, a former professor losing her memory. She half-remembers Edmund, calls him by another student's name, but hums fragments of Marta's sketches. He learns Ilse was Halina's last protégée with access to the archive. Emotional beat: tenderness tangled with suspicion; he can't tell if he's protecting Marta or himself.

chapters.title: Ilse
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins. Ilse Brandt, poised and ambitious, grants Edmund an interview assuming he's a journalist. She describes 'her' compositional process with details only someone inside Marta's world could know. Edmund says nothing of who he is. Emotional beat: a duel conducted entirely in courtesies; loyalty to the dead versus the pull of being seen again.

chapters.title: What the Night Janitor Hears
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Working nights, he overhears students rehearsing Ilse's published quartet and notices errors no one else could catch — places where performance tradition has overwritten Marta's intent. He corrects a student, then regrets it. Emotional beat: the dangerous pleasure of expertise returning, and the fear that using it makes him complicit in his own erasure.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Halina's POV, fragmenting. In a lucid hour, Halina gives Edmund Marta's final letter, unfinished, one sentence trailing off. She reveals Marta died the night after confronting Edmund about the scandal — and that Edmund's silence at that confrontation broke her. Emotional beat: devastation; the untranslatable sentence becomes legible, and it indicts him.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Locked Room
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. We learn Ilse didn't steal so much as salvage: Halina, forgetting, gave her the archive freely, and Ilse completed what Marta left unfinished. But she has let the credit stand alone. Confronted privately by Edmund, she offers him co-credit in exchange for silence about the archive's true origin. Emotional beat: temptation — a clean lie that would restore everything.

chapters.title: Rising Tension: The Premiere
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Ilse's quartet is programmed for the conservatory's centennial gala; Halina will be guest of honor, likely not remembering why it matters. Edmund drafts an exposé, then burns it, then writes it again. A student he mentored asks him, unknowingly, whether the janitor ever wanted to be more. Emotional beat: the cost of each choice made visible; time running out.

chapters.title: Climax: Both Names
chapters.summary: At the gala, as Ilse takes her bow, Edmund walks onto the stage in his janitor's uniform and tells the hall whose music they've heard — and what his own silence cost Marta. He sits at the piano and plays her unfinished coda, completing the sentence the letter couldn't. Emotional beat: exposure as release; truth chosen over the loyalty that protected only his shame.

chapters.title: Resolution: The Unsaid, Said
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Aftermath: professional ruin for some, unexpected grace for others — Ilse publicly shares the archive, Halina dies having heard her daughter's name spoken from a stage, and the students adopt Edmund as teacher-in-residence, the found family he never sought. Final image: he unlocks Hall C and leaves the door open. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging.
